title: My coworker joined our video call from home. Behind him was my kitchen, and my lights were on.
transcript:
My coworker joined our video call from home. Behind him was my kitchen, and my lights were on. It was a Monday morning meeting, eight people in little boxes. Dave from accounting joined late, apologizing, and I froze. Behind him was my kitchen. My yellow fridge. My fruit bowl with the one brown banana. My lights, which I'd turned off before I left for the office.

Dave lives three states away. I've never met him in person.

I messaged him privately. "Where are you working from today?" He typed back, "Home, why?"

I took a screenshot and zoomed in. On the fridge, under a magnet, was the grocery list I'd written that morning. The last item was crossed out. I hadn't crossed anything out.

I left the office and drove home. The front door was locked. The kitchen was dark, everything exactly where I'd left it. No one there.

I opened my laptop at the counter and rejoined the call, just to prove to myself I was being ridiculous.

Dave was still on. His background was still my kitchen. But now, behind his shoulder, I could see me, standing at the counter, staring into a laptop.

Dave smiled and leaned toward his camera.

"You're finally home," he said.
